title: Starting on clarinet and sitting in with George Lewis
summary: Dutre began on clarinet; the first man to let him play was George Lewis, who was with Rena at the time.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah. I wonder if you can tell us about your earliest days now in music when you started out. How old were you and what instrument did you start on?
Right on the clarinet? Yeah, I started on clarinet.
Well, during my time coming up, you would go up to a place and the fellow would say, Oh, boy, go home and let me ask you to kind of think about it. Yeah.
I've heard how they did that.
Well, the first fellow, that was very rare. The first fellow who gave me a chance to play a little was George Lewis. He was playing with René at the time.
And he said, go ahead, play, have your fun. I said, okay.
I played a couple numbers. I was so elated.
